core_obligations: Observe that finite projective R-modules are exactly the summands of finite free R-modules (proof line 13472), so the two categories have the same finite-projective objects on the section ring.

Define the forward functor E -> Gamma(C, E) (proof line 13474); for E a summand of a finite free O-module, Gamma(C, E) is a summand of the finite free R-module Gamma(C, O^n) = R^n (proof lines 13473-13474).

Give the inverse functor via the morphism of ringed topoi (f, f^#): (Sh(C), O) -> (Sh(pt), R) with f_* = global sections and f^{-1} the constant sheaf (proof lines 13475-13483); the inverse is f^*, and the two constructions are mutually inverse by construction.
proof_roadmap: Finite projective R-modules are summands of finite free R-modules.
Global sections sends summands of finite free O-modules to summands of finite free R-modules.
The constant-sheaf pullback of the morphism of ringed topoi gives the inverse functor f^*.
difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies, on a ringed site (C, O), the O-modules that are summands of finite free modules with the finite projective R-modules, R = Gamma(C, O) (statement lines 13461-13468). The proof (proof lines 13470-13484) is fully constructive: global sections gives the forward functor, and the inverse is f^* for f: (Sh(C), O) -> (Sh(pt), R) the morphism of ringed topoi with pushforward global sections and pullback the constant sheaf. H2: the content is the two-way construction over a morphism of ringed topoi; no long chain of verifications is needed. This is the site-level statement of which the analogous lemma in the chapter cohomology.tex (ringed spaces) is a special case; the site version is the more general one and is the one counted here.
